question: A 54-year-old man is brought to the emergency after experiencing several syncopal episodes. The patient states that he is currently taking erythromycin for treatment of bronchitis and another medication for treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). If an electrocardiogram reveals torsades de pointes, the patient is most likely taking which of the following medications for treatment of his reflux disease?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Erythromycin" -> "inhibits cytochrome P450 enzymes" -> "increased plasma levels of certain drugs" -> "Cisapride" -> "prolongation of QT interval" -> "torsades de pointes" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Famotidine" -> "H2 receptor antagonist" -> "no significant effect on cytochrome P450 enzymes" -> "no known association with QT interval prolongation" -> "unlikely to cause torsades de pointes" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Lansoprazole" -> "proton pump inhibitor" -> "minimal inhibition of cytochrome P450 enzymes" -> "no significant effect on QT interval" -> "unlikely to cause torsades de pointes" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Metoclopramide" -> "dopamine receptor antagonist" -> "can cause QT prolongation" -> "possible risk of torsades de pointes" -> "less likely than Cisapride" -> 70%
analysis: Cisapride is known to prolong the QT interval on an electrocardiogram, which can lead to torsades de pointes, a type of ventricular tachycardia. Erythromycin, an antibiotic the patient is taking, also has the potential to prolong the QT interval. The combination of erythromycin and cisapride can significantly increase the risk of developing torsades de pointes due to additive effects on QT prolongation. The other medications listed (Famotidine, Lansoprazole, and Metoclopramide) are less likely to cause QT prolongation compared to Cisapride.
